title: How to choose Aida fabric for cross-stitch
subtitle: Matching fabric count to design complexity, finished size, and skill level
excerpt: Aida count determines both the physical size of the finished piece and how fine the stitches look. Lower counts (11ct) give large, visible stitches on a bigger canvas; higher counts (18ct) give fine detail in a smaller space. The count choice is set by what the chart requires and how confident you are with small work.
sourceNotes: Fabric count conventions from Aida manufacturer guidelines. Standard cross-stitch fabric guidance from Weldon's Practical Needlework series (1880s), Internet Archive.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. Sold by count (squares per inch): 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the most common.

content.text: count is the number of squares per inch. A 14-count Aida has 14 squares per inch in each direction; a chart stitched on it produces a stitch that is about 1.8 mm across. Choose a higher count for smaller, finer work and a lower count for larger, more visible stitches.

Most printed charts specify a count or give the finished dimensions at a recommended count. If a chart says "14ct Aida, 15 x 20 cm", using 18ct Aida would produce the same design at roughly 11 x 15 cm. The design looks finer and smaller but the stitch count is unchanged.
Common Aida counts and their uses

11-count Aida produces the largest stitches and is the easiest to see. Good for beginners and for projects intended to be seen from a distance: a large wall hanging, a tote bag, or a kit for a child. Each stitch is about 2.3 mm across. Use three strands of floss for solid coverage at this count.

14-count Aida is the default for most charts and kits. Two strands of floss give even coverage. Stitches are clear and easy to see, and a small detailed design fits on a manageable piece of fabric. Most starter kits use 14-count.

16-count Aida is a step up in fineness. Stitches are smaller and the finished piece is more detailed at the same stitch count. Still comfortable for good eyesight without magnification. Use two strands.

18-count Aida produces fine detail in a small space. Good for miniature work, small ornaments, or designs with very fine lines and gradients. Consider a magnifier at this count, especially in poor light. Use two strands; one strand on some specialty designs.

items.symptom: The finished size is much larger or smaller than expected
items.cause: The fabric count used does not match what the chart specified.
items.fix: Calculate the finished size before cutting: (stitch count in one direction) divided by (fabric count) gives the dimension in inches. At 14ct, a chart that is 140 stitches wide produces a design 10 inches wide.

items.symptom: Two strands of floss don't cover the fabric at the chosen count
items.cause: At 11ct, two strands are too thin and the fabric ground shows through.
items.fix: Use three strands at 11ct Aida. At 14ct and above, two strands give even coverage with the correct fabric tension.

content.text: Try the same small chart on 14ct and 16ct Aida and compare the results side by side. The same stitch count at a higher count fits in a smaller space and reads as more detailed work, even though you made exactly the same moves.
